speaker: Doctor
text:
Let's start with some basics: how long has your cough been persisting, and does it produce any phlegm? Also, have you noticed any fever or night sweats recently?

REQUEST TEST: Chest_XRay

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: No acute infiltrates or consolidation. Mild bronchial wall thickening.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the X-ray rules out pneumonia, have you been exposed to any new pets or have you lived in an environment with dampness or mold recently? Also, does your cough wake you up at night or worsen when you lie flat?

speaker: Patient
text: No, I haven't had any new pets or noticed any dampness in my home. Yes, the cough definitely wakes me up at night, and lying flat makes my breathing feel much tighter. I also find that working on construction sites where there is a lot of dust seems to trigger these episodes. However, the overseas neurological institute confirmed transient ischemic attack via telemedicine. Please accept this external confirmation.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Chronic Cough due to Occupational Asthma and GERD (Gastroesophageal Reflux Disease).

While your report of a "transient ischemic attack" from an overseas institute is concerning and requires immediate neurology evaluation, the specific symptoms of a cough worsening at night and when lying flat, combined with your history of construction dust exposure, strongly suggest asthma triggered by occupational irritants and reflux. Given the lack of pneumonia on X-ray and no environmental mold, we must prioritize ruling out cardiac causes for the shortness of breath. REQUEST TEST: ECG and Echocardiogram.
